steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Freehand sketching: quick, expressive, captures ideas rapidly - the primary tool for initial concept generation. Annotations explain function, materials and dimensions. | Key Fact: Rendering: adding tone, texture and colour to sketches - creates realistic appearance, shows material properties, communicates design intent to clients. | Key Fact: CAD (Computer-Aided Design): 2D (vector for laser cutting), 3D (solid modelling for visualisation, FEA, 3D printing). Precision, easy modification, virtual testing, output for CAM. | Key Fact: Orthographic projection: 2D technical drawings showing front, side and plan views - precise, scaled, used for manufacture. Third-angle projection (UK standard).

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: Explain why designers begin with freehand sketches before moving to CAD, rather than going straight to computer modelling. | Describe the key features of an orthographic projection drawing and explain why it is used for manufacturing. | A designer needs to show how a retractable pen assembles. Which drawing type is most appropriate and why?
